questions: How representative was the beta: how many users, what share of them were on the checkout path under real sale-level traffic, and did the 8% conversion lift come from an A/B comparison or from a before-and-after comparison that other factors could explain?

What is your actual timeline: if app store review takes a day or several and you ship now, would approval, release and adoption by users all land before the sale starts, and how many of the 2 million users will be on the new version when the push notification goes out?

If the new checkout fails during the sale, how fast could you stop the damage: do you have a server-side feature flag or remote kill switch to return to the old checkout without shipping an app update?
Can you roll out the new checkout gradually, for example to 5 to 10 percent of users via a flag or staged release, so you capture much of the gain while limiting exposure?

How well has the backend been tested for sale-level load, including the payment provider, inventory and order systems, which the beta likely never stressed, and what has changed on the server side for this checkout?

How does the crash dashboard's 'as stable as the current build' cover non-crash failures such as payment errors, stuck screens, wrong totals, failed promo codes or issues on older devices and OS versions?
What would a failure cost compared with the gain: roughly how much is sale-week revenue times an 8% lift versus the revenue lost per hour of a checkout outage during the push-driven peak?

What would waiting cost in practice: does a launch after the sale lose only the sale-week lift, or are there other reasons (competitors, marketing commitments, features tied to the new checkout) to ship before it?

Is there a third option, such as shipping now to a small cohort or after a freeze of two to three days before the sale, or shipping the new checkout but keeping the old one as the default for the first sale hours?

Who is on call and ready during the sale window, and are monitoring and alerts for checkout success rate, payment errors and latency in place so a problem would be seen within minutes rather than hours?
